items.excerpt: Figma's Sightlines no.2 collects what design and product leaders at Cisco, OpenAI and Airbnb have learned about designing agentic products. It is a leadership-level read on how design orgs restructure when the thing you ship is an agent, not a screen.

Apps and agents built in v0 can now securely connect to 100+ third-party services — Slack, Google, Notion, GitHub, Salesforce — through Vercel Connect. Prompt-built prototypes can now reach real company data without a developer wiring the auth.

Top-down AI mandates raise output expectations but not real productivity: nearly 40% of the speed gain is eaten by verification and coordination work. The argument is that AI has to live inside the workflow teams already use, not sit beside it as another handoff.

A practitioner's sweep of the AI design tool stack as it stands in late 2026, framed around the blank-canvas-with-a-three-hour-deadline case. Useful as a map of which tool actually earns a slot in a working designer's day.

Auto layout gains "Around" and "Evenly" spacing alongside a renamed "Between", matching how CSS distributes space. Small on the surface, but it closes another gap between what a designer draws and what an agent or engineer can generate as code.

Scantic is a free iOS app that captures footage and trains a 3D Gaussian Splat in under a minute — entirely on-device, with no cloud upload. Photoreal 3D capture stops being a pipeline step and becomes something you do while standing in front of the object.

Foundry's Nuke 17.1 adds relighting for Gaussian splats and Hydra 2.0 support in the 3D viewer. Neural-captured scenes become relightable comp elements, pulling AI-era 3D capture into a standard finishing workflow.

Runway, Kling, Pika, Luma and Google Flow/Veo compared not on demo reels but on usable-shot rate and cost per delivered shot, with a test protocol you can run on your own assets. It reframes gen-video budgeting around failures, not generations.

Onshape Labs' new FeatureScript MCP server lets any AI coding agent — Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT — build, test and evaluate custom CAD features. Custom tooling inside CAD moves from a specialist task to a prompt.

Pudu's MP2000 pallet robot carries a 2,000 kg payload and uses AI-native perception for floor-to-floor material transport. A concrete look at how physical-AI perception is now designed into industrial hardware rather than bolted on.
Block's free open-source desktop app Bird unifies Claude, Codex, Copilot, Amp and Goose behind one interface. For design engineers juggling agents, it is a single surface instead of five terminals.

A hands-on comparison of Lovable, Replit, Bolt, Codex and Claude Code, matched to the kind of app idea each one actually suits. Practical triage for designers deciding where a prototype should be born.

DeepSeek V4 Flash with image input is now callable through Vercel AI Gateway on one API key, with a 1M-token context window, fallbacks and per-request tracing. Cheap multimodal vision for screenshot-to-UI and design-QA agents.

Slack Code embeds coding agents like Claude Code and Devin directly into team channels, turning agent work from a solo terminal session into something a whole team watches, steers and approves. Designers and PMs get a seat at the build loop.

NanoClaw's Slack integration spins up persistent teams of specialized AI agents with their own identities and skills from a single message, and lets one person's agent query another's. A preview of what a design org staffed partly by agents looks like.

D&AD's 2026 AI and Creativity Report warns the industry is cutting exactly the roles and craft that AI cannot replace. A data point for anyone arguing headcount policy inside a creative org right now.

An argument that AI ethics in product is really an accountability gradient: making the human behind the machine visible changes what users judge as right. Directly actionable for anyone designing disclosure and attribution in AI features.
Rejects the "AI kills software" framing in favour of evolution: interfaces, not apps, are what get replaced. A useful lens for product designers planning what their surface even is in two years.

A product designer walks through building motion design plugins for Figma himself in Figma's Show Your Work series. The clearest current example of designers shipping their own tooling instead of filing a request.
Matt Wolfe digs into Claude's text watermark and how far it can travel once content leaves the model. Provenance marking is about to become a real constraint on how creative teams reuse AI output.
A case study on how Searchable turns a customer request into a shipped feature in about 30 minutes on Vercel. Concrete evidence of what the prompt-to-production loop compresses in practice.
